part.text:
I found the issue. This app uses Next.js 16 with `cacheComponents: true` (Partial Prerendering / PPR). The product page awaits `getInventory()` — which calls the dynamic `connection()` API — directly in the component body before returning any JSX. This blocks the entire page render, so even the static `<h1>` title can't be served until the dynamic data resolves.

The fix is to split the page into a static shell (the title) and a dynamic part wrapped in `<Suspense>`. The static shell prerenders and appears immediately on navigation; the inventory streams in afterward.
Now let me verify it typechecks and builds.
Typecheck passes. Let me run the build to confirm PPR splits the static shell correctly.

part.text:
The build confirms the fix. The `/product` route is now marked `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — previously it would have been fully dynamic (`ƒ`) because the `await getInventory()` call (which invokes the dynamic `connection()` API) blocked the whole page render with no Suspense boundary. **What changed** (`app/product/page.tsx`): Extracted the dynamic inventory fetch into an `Inventory` async component wrapped in ``, while keeping the `

Premium Widget

` title in the static shell. **Result:** On navigation from home, the static shell — including the title — is served from the prerendered HTML immediately, and the inventory data streams in afterward via the Suspense boundary.
